notes: The voice is sharp and self-aware with genuine wit, but it leans more toward mid-century essayist irony (think E.B. White or even early David Sedaris) than Parker specifically — her style was more compressed, more venomous, and less given to extended structural metaphors; the usability suffers slightly because the self-consciousness of the prose may read as precious to a busy recipient, though the core pitch survives intact.
